### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

completion

### Description

I already created the issue #882 about having $0 after completion.
I also then created an issue on LSP side where they [explained](https://github.com/mrcjkb/rustaceanvim/discussions/394#discussioncomment-9459398) that this is what is coming to Neovim 0.10 natively.

But mini.completion isn't supporting snippets, correct? if so, would you be open to support it or accept PR? currently I have no idea about volume of work to be done for it, but sound interesting and might help me get familiar with all this Lua madness.

Thanks for the suggestion!

Yes, [this is planned](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/574#issuecomment-1819531525) after the release of 'mini.snippets'. As 0.10 is released, this will now be possible to start working on. Yet, no concrete plans.

I appreciated the suggestion, but 'mini.completion' is one of the messiest module in 'mini.nvim' and I'll tackle it myself.

Let's have this issue open so as an extra measure to not forget about it.
@echasnovski can the 0.11 LSP completion side effects api be used for this?

> @echasnovski can the 0.11 LSP completion side effects api be used for this?

I am afraid I am not really sure what you're referring to. Could you link to it, please?

But if it is only 0.11, then it probably won't be used as I'd like 'mini.nvim' (and snippet support in 'mini.completion') to support as many versions as possible. Right now it should be possible to support 0.10+ but maybe after 'mini.snippets' this can get better.

Oh, turns out this wasn't actually added in 0.11

I was referring to the `vim.lsp.util.apply_text_edits` function. It seems like unless you need to have custom snippet support then using it together with the new snippets API should provide a very simple way to expand most existing LSP completions?

> I was referring to the `vim.lsp.util.apply_text_edits` function. It seems like unless you need to have custom snippet support then using it together with the new snippets API should provide a very simple way to expand most existing LSP completions?

I *think* just using `vim.snippet` should be enough. It is just that resolving this issue is intentionally postponed after 'mini.snippets' is a thing. So that I'd have more knowledge about snippets and can be sure that I've tried to support as many previous Neovim versions as possible.

> A lot of the functionality of mini.completion is duplicating the functionality added in core with `vim.lsp.completion`. The main difference is that mini.completion has proper auto complete, while built-in is only activated on trigger chars.

Purely due to how time works, I'd like to think that it is `vim.lsp.completion` which is duplicating 'mini.completion' functionality :) Although it used 'mfussenegger/nvim-lsp-compl' as a reference :) Or a more neutral "they share similar functionality" is even better.

> So perhaps, when 0.11 is released, it would make sense to refactor that plugin to remove all of the custom popup menu item building and rely on `vim.lsp.completion.trigger()` instead? This would simplify the code, fit the plugin's goal of using as much native stuff as possible, and, as an additional benefit, bring support for snippets and stuff for free.

Although motivation is sound, there are several crucial problems:
- 'mini.nvim' does not only support latest stable, but also two (minor) versions prior. So it will be not until the release of Neovim 0.13 when 'mini.completion' can be rewritten to use `vim.lsp.completion`.
- One *big* thing that I'd taken into account was that completion candidates persist across deleting characters. I.e. after completion candidates are shown, pressing `<BS>` should still show them with possibly bigger set of matched candidates. This is not the case with `vim.lsp.completion` (as far as my experiments and looking at its code showed) and I am not sure if it will be. Supporting this use case is one of the main reasons why 'mini.completion' uses 'omnifunc' and 'completefunc' approach instead of relying on `vim.fn.complete()` (which is what `vim.lsp.completion` currently uses).

> Purely due to how time works, I'd like to think that it is vim.lsp.completion which is duplicating 'mini.completion' functionality :) Although it used 'mfussenegger/nvim-lsp-compl' as a reference :) Or a more neutral "they share similar functionality" is even better.

I didn't mean that in the sense that you stole the functionality or anything like that :) I purely meant that by installing mini.completion you're now introducing extra code logic duplication. In the same sense I'd say that mini.comment is duplicating the functionality of built-in commenting, despite the fact that the built-in feature was implemented by you and based on mini.comment.

> One big thing that I'd taken into account was that completion candidates persist across deleting characters

I see, that makes sense. Perhaps when 0.11 is released you should add this note to the "difference from alternatives" section in the mini.completion docs?

The reason I asked is that I was playing around with native LSP completion and realized that the only things it lacks for me are pretty colors and proper autocompletion. With the ability to set pretty colors now being implemented (https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/30060), I was wondering if there could be a plugin that simply adds autocomplete logic on top of native completion.

But I guess just adding an autocmd with a few checks and a timer is enough for basic autocomplete, and it sounds simple enough that I could just do it in my nvim config without a plugin.

> ... purely meant that by installing mini.completion you're now introducing extra code logic duplication.

The overlap is not that big, I'd say, and it was already present from 'mini.completion' start (as its core initially was similar to `vim.lsp.omnifunc`). The "autotrigger" parts are quite different.

> In the same sense I'd say that mini.comment is duplicating the functionality of built-in commenting, despite the fact that the built-in feature was implemented by you and based on mini.comment.

Yeah, unfortunately, no good way to reuse built-in commenting because there is no exported Lua functions by design (otherwise no merge would happen). 'mini.comment' still offers more on top, though.

> The reason I asked is that I was playing around with native LSP completion and realized that the only things it lacks for me are pretty colors and proper autocompletion.

Fallback to built-in "usual" completion is a big part of 'mini.completion' and was one of the goals of even creating it. Because not every buffer has LSP attached to it yet autocompletion is still useful.

> With the ability to set pretty colors now being implemented ([neovim/neovim#30060](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/30060)), I was wondering if there could be a plugin that simply adds autocomplete logic on top of native completion.

@flexagoon, 'mini.completion' now by default highlights LSP kind (with `kind_hlgroup`) on Neovim>=0.11 if 'mini.icons' is enabled. It uses highlight groups from its ["lsp" category](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/57e47cf7a2923684e7413989ab267ed9730e7d03/doc/mini-icons.txt#L411). This requires enabling 'mini.icons', but I think it is a good alternative to possibly allowing customizing that highlighting in `MiniCompletion.config`. And I also don't really like the idea of something like `convert` from the `vim.lsp.completion.BufferOpts` as there is already a `MiniCompletion.config.lsp_completion.process_items` (which doesn't allow overriding `kind_hlgroup`, but I think it can be added if there is a demand).

All in all, thanks for the tip about the new `hl_group` and `kind_hlgroup` fields in completion items!

> And I also don't really like the idea of something like `convert` from the `vim.lsp.completion.BufferOpts` as there is already a `MiniCompletion.config.lsp_completion.process_items` (which doesn't allow overriding `kind_hlgroup`, but I think it can be added if there is a demand).

After sleeping on it, allowing `config.lsp_completion.process_items` to set `kind_hlgroup` **is** the cleaner solution. The default 'mini.icons' one is shuffled to `MiniCompletion.default_process_items()` and still works as default (if 'mini.icons' is enabled). This should now be the part of `main`.

```lua
local keys = {

	["ctrl-y"] = vim.api.nvim_replace_termcodes("<C-y>", true, true, true),
```

Does MiniSnippets provide an API where I can see if I'm in an active MiniSnippet session and call a function to jump to next tabstop?

> Does MiniSnippets provide an API where I can see if I'm in an active MiniSnippet session and call a function to jump to next tabstop?

Yep. Try replacing ...

```lua
	elseif vim.snippet.active({ direction = 1 }) then
		return '<cmd>lua vim.snippet.jump(1)<cr>'
```

with this:

```lua
	elseif MiniSnippets.session.get() ~= nil then
		return '<cmd>lua MiniSnippets.session.jump("next")<cr>'
```

Hmmm... Then judging by [LSP specification](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#completionItem), this is not a snippet. A snippet is defined in exactly two ways: either by kind (should be 15; 2 is for "Method") or by `InsertTextFormat` (should be present and equal to 2). I don't think deviating from this specification is a good idea; especially by treating a snippet any item that has tabstop-like text in it.

Or is there an `insertTextFormat` set to 2 in the whole `CompletionList` response (one step higher with respect to nesting)?

Respecting the `textEditText` is a good idea, though. I'll take a look.

As a [reference](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/092529ebbf6fe566399aa47c274d708b8dea5334/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/completion.lua#L146-L189), neovim built-in completion also handles completion word using this priority order. > Can I ask you to consider this again? because I can't find a way to fix this outside the mini.completion, and it might be the standard way to deal with `word`. As a [reference](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/092529ebbf6fe566399aa47c274d708b8dea5334/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/completion.lua#L146-L189), neovim built-in completion also handles completion word using this priority order. The author also refer this [lsp specification](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#textDocument_completion)

I don't think there is a need to fix anything here. [This line](https://github.com/wenjinnn/mini.nvim/blob/e1089e481ed62f7fbcf2ce3c9e42889ba4cb1760/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1006) is intended to only set `word` temporarily because `word` is a required field for Neovim's completion item. It defines a word which will be inserted during up-down navigation across completion items.

The actual snippet text is computed [later](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/d7ba1dec0082b7a542aa79c327e9554d4a27cc2c/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1077) (as there might be updates from `completionItem/resolve`) and `insertText` [*is* used there to find the actual snippet text](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/d7ba1dec0082b7a542aa79c327e9554d4a27cc2c/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1068). Preferring text from `textEdit` over `insertText` [is according to spec](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#completionItem) ("... Therefore it is recommended to use `textEdit` instead since it avoids additional client side interpretation." as a part of `insertText` description).

So for [this server response](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/886#issuecomment-2707989215) the `valueOf(double d) : String` (i.e. `label`) will be used in popup menu and when navigating up-down completion list while `valueOf(${1:0})` (i.e. `textEditText`) will be used as snippet text.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94e3ba2d-87a6-4c43-a691-6041055a115d)

> ... but my case is once I didn't apply current selected item but choose to return to normal mode, the selected text will leave there, Unless I have `noinsert` in `completeopt`.

This is an intended behavior with the following reasoning:
- There is no item selected when popup is shown (as 'noselect' is set in 'completeopt' in `require('mini.completion').setup()`). So selecting an item is treated as an intended action from the user.
- Selecting an item with snippet text is temporary because snippet should be actually inserted, which ends a completion. Inserting is a separate action done after `<C-y>` or non-keyword character. There is no good reason to support inserting "temporary" text as permanent for snippet text items because LSP server said that that item should be inserted as snippet.
- If you want remove inserted text and end a completion (even before exiting into Normal mode), [press `<C-e>` for that](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/d7ba1dec0082b7a542aa79c327e9554d4a27cc2c/doc/mini-completion.txt#L94-L95).

Finally got around to migrate to mini.snippets. So far it's a blast!
So much more convenient than convoluted luasnip syntax.

For anyone still subscribed to this issue, there is now (finally) a way to expose snippets collected/prepared/loaded by 'mini.snippets' to (auto)completion engines like 'mini.completion': add a [`MiniSnippets.start_lsp_server()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/6be765891c95242f6b8ebd3a25aa285ab3e9f6de/doc/mini-snippets.txt#L1240) call after `require('mini.snippets').setup()`. This will start a dedicated LSP server for 'mini.snippets' which will provide its collected snippets as completion suggestions.
